title.en: Modern periodic law and periodic trends
Why does argon sit before potassium?

text.en: Argon is heavier than potassium, yet it is placed before it in the periodic table. Mendeleev's table, which went by atomic mass, could not explain this. The answer came from a deeper property of the atom - the number of protons.

In 1912 Henry Moseley showed that atomic number, the number of protons in the nucleus, is the real basis for arranging elements, not atomic mass.
Modern periodic law: the physical and chemical properties of the elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
The 118 known elements are arranged in 7 horizontal rows called periods and 18 vertical columns called groups.
Period 1 has 2 elements, periods 2 and 3 have 8 each, periods 4 and 5 have 18 each, and periods 6 and 7 have 32 each.
Elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons, so they have the same valency and similar chemical properties; group 1 are alkali metals, group 2 alkaline earth metals, group 17 halogens and group 18 noble gases.
Atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus to the outermost shell. It decreases along a period because the nuclear charge grows while the number of shells stays the same, and it increases down a group because new shells are added.
A cation is smaller than its atom and an anion is larger than its atom. Ionic radii follow the same period and group trends.
Ionisation energy is the minimum energy needed to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom. It increases along a period and decreases down a group.
Electron affinity is the energy released when a gaseous atom gains an electron; electronegativity is the tendency to attract the shared pair of electrons in a bond, and both increase along a period and decrease down a group.
On the Pauling scale the electronegativity difference tells the bond type: a difference above 1.7 means mainly ionic, below 1.7 mainly covalent.

problem.en: Predict the nature of the bond in NaCl using Pauling electronegativities Na = 1.0 and Cl = 3.0.

why.en: Subtract the smaller electronegativity from the larger.

text.en: So the bond is mainly ionic - sodium gives its electron to chlorine.

prompt.en: Explain why atomic radius decreases across a period but increases down a group.

requiredIdeas.en: Nuclear charge increases along a period
New shells are added down a group
Valence electrons are pulled closer or held farther

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking more electrons always means a bigger atom (across a period the shell number is the same)

points.en: Modern periodic law uses atomic number (Moseley, 1912).
7 periods and 18 groups; group members share valence electrons.
Along a period: radius decreases; ionisation energy, electron affinity and electronegativity increase.
Down a group: radius increases; the other three decrease.
Electronegativity difference above 1.7 means an ionic bond.
